angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 403,506 km at 92.45 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.8167 +/- 0.0141 mas (same row, RUWE 1.27): 92.45 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.58 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Gomez Barrientos et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5736 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...99G/abstract): 403,506 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.57 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Gomez Barrientos et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5736 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...99G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3949 +/- 157 K from Gomez Barrientos et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5736 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...99G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Gomez Barrientos et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5736 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...99G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5736.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.667, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5736 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.1332, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, UCAC4 698-056156: projected rotation speed 2.03 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2022ApJS..259...35A)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
